decisions.rationale: Kingambit's Steel typing resists Fairy, safely handling Calm Mind Floette, while Kowtow Cleave shuts down setup. Froslass provides essential Thunder Wave paralysis to lock down Unburden Sneasler. Lycanroc-Dusk and Basculegion offer spread Rock Slide and Adaptability STAB respectively, creating a balanced roster with speed control, Intimidate mitigation, and matchup versatility.
decisions.notebook: Opponent relies on Unburden Sneasler + Incineroar Intimidate core. Prioritize paralysis/priority to neutralize Unburden activation. Kingambit counters Floette; Froslass enables Snow/Mega for speed control. Be mindful of Last Respects targeting low-HP/weather setters. Maintain team structure for upcoming rounds.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion (1) is the primary Froslass-Mega check via Last Respects super effectiveness. Incineroar (4) provides Intimidate support and FlareBlitz coverage against Rock/Dark/Steel threats. Sinistcha (5) offers RagePowder redirect and MatchaGotcha spread damage. Floette-Eternal (3) brings Flowerveil status immunity and DazzlingGleam coverage. This team avoids the Sneasler mirror and Kingambit redundancy while covering Froslass-Mega, Lycanroc-Dusk, and Scovillain.
decisions.notebook: Opponent likely leads Froslass-Mega with Snowscape; Last Respects on Basculegion is the primary check. Opponent Sneasler uses Close Combat aggressively dropping Defense by 2; resisted Close Combat can still KO it. Opponent Kingambit is weak to Last Respects and Close Combat. Opponent Lycanroc-Dusk uses Rock Slide/Accelerock with Focus Sash; Water/Ghost coverage handles it. Opponent Scovillain has Overheat and Giga Drain; Ghost/Fairy coverage handles it. Avoid bringing both Kingambits; ensure a dedicated Sneasler check with bulky Water or Psychic types. Froslass-Mega lead is common opener; have Last Respects ready on Basculegion.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion's Choice Scarf guarantees it moves first. Kowtow Cleave applies a vital -2 Attack drop to Basculegion, drastically reducing the threat of its WaveCrash while dealing super-effective damage. Froslass Protects to safely weather the turn, preserving its bulk and speed control without wasting its Mega Stone prematurely. This setup neutralizes immediate pressure and sets up favorable matchups for the rest of the match.

Basculegion (Speed 214) outspeeds Kingambit (70-102) and Last Respects is Ghost-type super effective (2x) against Dark/Steel, removing the primary physical threat that already has Attack +1 and Defiant. Incineroar uses Helping Hand on Basculegion to boost next-turn damage, avoiding the risk of Incineroar being hit first by Froslass-Mega's special attacks since Incineroar (Speed 104) is slower than Froslass-Mega (Speed 154-189).
decisions.notebook: Opponent likely runs Froslass-Mega lead with Snowscape; Last Respects on Basculegion is the primary check. Kingambit with Attack +1 and Defiant is the biggest immediate threat - remove it first. Sneasler uses Close Combat aggressively dropping Defense by 2; resisted Close Combat can still KO it. Ensure a dedicated Sneasler check with bulky Water or Psychic types. Do not bring both Kingambits.

decisions.rationale: Basculegion is fainted and must be switched out. Sinistcha (option 0) is the correct switch target because its Grass/Ghost typing makes it neutral to Blizzard (Grass resists Ice at 0.5x, Ghost resists Ice at 0.5x, net 1x), which is critical if Froslass Mega Evolves and sets Snowscape. Sinistcha also has Focus Sash for guaranteed survival, Rage Powder to redirect attacks away from allies, and Ghost STAB in Shadow Ball. Floette-Eternal is 2x weak to Ice, making it dangerously vulnerable to Froslass's Blizzard under Snowscape. Incineroar passes as it has no other actionable option.
decisions.notebook: Opponent likely runs Froslass-Mega lead with Snowscape; Last Respects on Basculegion is the primary check. Kingambit with Attack +1 and Defiant is the biggest immediate threat - remove it first. Sneasler uses Close Combat aggressively dropping Defense by 2; resisted Close Combat can still KO it. Ensure a dedicated Sneasler check with bulky Water or Psychic types. Do not bring both Kingambits. Sinistcha is a safer switch than Floette-Eternal due to Ice neutrality and Focus Sash survivability against potential Froslass-Mega Snowscape Blizzard.

decisions.rationale: Mega Evolving Froslass sets hail immediately, guaranteeing Blizzard's accuracy and applying spread pressure to both foes while setting up weather damage to break Sinistcha's Focus Sash next turn. Kingambit's Kowtow Cleave delivers a guaranteed super-effective hit that ignores Sinistcha's defenses, securing the knockout. This combination maximizes immediate damage output and establishes field control.

Both active Pokémon fainted, necessitating switches. Lycanroc-Dusk's high Speed and priority move will safely eliminate the nearly-fainted Sinistcha, while Basculegion pressures Incineroar. Securing this win clinches the series.

Shadow Ball on Froslass (2x effective, Ghost vs Ice/Ghost) and Flare Blitz on Kingambit (2x effective, Fire vs Dark/Steel) both hit super-effectively. Incineroar (Speed 104) moves before Sinistcha (Speed 90), so Flare Blitz lands first to pressure Kingambit—the biggest immediate threat with Attack +1 and Defiant—while Shadow Ball follows on Froslass. This maximizes damage to both foes simultaneously.
decisions.notebook: Kingambit with Defiant and Atk +1 is the primary threat; remove it first with super-effective Fire moves. Froslass is frail and weak to Ghost; Shadow Ball can KO it. Avoid Parting Shot on Kingambit (Defiant raises Atk when stats drop). Do not switch Sinistcha unless necessary—Focus Sash and Ice neutrality make it a safe switch-in. Floette-Eternal is faster but lacks resistances to Kingambit's STAB.

decisions.rationale: Rock Slide eliminates the 1% Sinistcha and heavily damages Incineroar simultaneously. Basculegion follows up with Wave Crash to secure the KO on Incineroar, clearing the field and winning the match.

Sinistcha uses Matcha Gotcha (spread Grass) to hit both remaining foes super-effectively (2x vs Rock and 2x vs Water/Ghost), maximizing damage output with its 190 SpA Modest spread. Incineroar targets Basculegion with Flare Blitz because Basculegion's Last Respects (Ghost) is super-effective against Sinistcha and Wave Crash (Water) is super-effective against Incineroar, making Basculegion the more urgent threat to neutralize. Both moves are committed simultaneously; Incineroar's higher Speed (104 vs 90) means it acts first in the turn.
decisions.notebook: Kingambit and Froslass-Mega are both removed; the remaining foe threats are Lycanroc-Dusk (Rock, physical attacker) and Basculegion (Water/Ghost, physical attacker with Last Respects super-effective vs Ghost types). Sinistcha at 1% HP is extremely fragile—Matcha Gotcha must secure a KO or it will likely faint next turn. Snowscape (Hail) deals damage to non-Ice types each turn; Floette-Eternal (Fairy) takes Hail damage. If Sinistcha faints, Floette must come in and needs to handle Rock and Water/Ghost threats—consider Ice-type coverage or Protect to stall Hail damage. Watch for Lycanroc-Dusk's Accelerock (priority Rock) which can OHKO frail targets.

decisions.rationale: Both Sinistcha and Incineroar are fainted. Floette-Eternal is the only remaining replacement. Slot b (Incineroar's position, facing Basculegion) is the better placement: Floette at Speed 158 is faster than Basculegion's 98-130 range, so Floette moves first and can use drainingkiss for healing or calmmind to boost defenses. Slot a (facing Lycanroc-Dusk) is a death sentence—Lycanroc's Accelerock (priority Rock) or Rock Slide (2x super effective spread) will almost certainly OHKO Floette. Therefore, switch Floette into slot b and pass on slot a.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Eternal (Fairy, Speed 158, flowerveil) is the sole remaining team member. It is weak to Rock (2x, dangerous vs Lycanroc-Dusk) and weak to Ghost Last Respects (2x, dangerous vs Basculegion) but has drainingkiss for sustain. Prioritize keeping Floette alive against Basculegion where Floette is speed-advantageous; avoid the Lycanroc-Dusk matchup entirely due to Accelerock priority Rock OHKO threat. Snowscape (Hail) deals residual damage to Floette each turn; factor this into longevity calculations.

decisions.rationale: Lycanroc uses priority Accelerock to safely chip Floette-Eternal before it can act, leveraging its higher Speed. Basculegion fires Last Respects, which scales massively due to two fainted allies and Adaptability, guaranteeing a knockout against Floette's frail bulk. Attacking is necessary to prevent Floette from setting up Calm Mind or healing.

Sinistcha is fainted and can only Pass. Floette-Eternal faces an Accelerock priority Rock OHKO from Lycanroc-Dusk, so it must Protect to survive; adding Mega Evolve grants stat boosts for future turns while the Protect shields from both foes' attacks. All non-Protect options result in Floette fainting before it can move due to Accelerock's priority.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Eternal is the sole surviving team member; it is weak to Rock (2x, OHKO threat from Lycanroc-Dusk Accelerock) and Ghost (2x, Last Respects from Basculegion). Accelerock always moves first due to priority +1, so Floette cannot attack before fainting without Protect. Snowscape residual damage should be factored into longevity. Mega Evolution stat boosts are valuable for future turns if Floette survives.

decisions.rationale: Opponent's roster is depleted to a single Floette-Mega. Basculegion's Wave Crash, boosted by Adaptability and Mystic Water, offers the highest probability of securing an OHKO or leaving Floette critically wounded. Lycanroc's Close Combat applies essential chip damage despite the resistance, leveraging Tough Claws. Focus Sash safely absorbs any retaliation if the KO fails. Passing or using spread moves squanders momentum against an isolated, vulnerable target.
decisions.notebook: Opponent team reduced to Floette-Mega. Prioritize aggressive physical damage to clinch match. Anticipate potential Sneasler/Kingambit entries in future rounds. Maintain focus on speed control and priority usage against Unburden cores.

selection: Protect [success rate reduced: Protected last turn]
decisions.rationale: Sinistcha is fainted (HP 0%) and can only Pass or Forfeit; passing keeps the game alive. Floette-Mega is the sole surviving Pokémon facing two active foes. Lycanroc-Dusk's Accelerock has priority +1 and always moves before Floette, making it an OHKO threat that cannot be outsped or KO'd in one hit (Dazzling Gleam is 0.5x effective against Rock and won't break Focus Sash). Protecting is the only way to survive this turn; despite the reduced success rate from protecting last turn, it is strictly better than attacking (which guarantees Floette faints to Accelerock next turn). If Protect succeeds, Floette survives into Turn 6 when Snowscape ends, gaining a free turn to set up or attack.
decisions.notebook: Floette-Eternal is the sole surviving team member; weak to Rock (2x, OHKO threat from Lycanroc-Dusk Accelerock) and Ghost (2x, Last Respects from Basculegion). Accelerock always moves first due to priority +1, so Floette cannot attack before fainting without Protect. Snowscape residual damage should be factored into longevity. Mega Evolution stat boosts are valuable for future turns if Floette survives. Protect success rate is reduced after protecting last turn; weigh against certain death from unprotected Accelerock.

reflections.summary: The series was won because the team-preview plan perfectly countered the opponent's core composition. Bringing Froslass-Mega, Kingambit, Basculegion, Lycanroc-Dusk, and Incineroar provided ideal weather control, early Defiant pressure, and late-game physical wallbreakers. Evolving Froslassite was correct, as Snowscape amplified Blizzard's coverage against their fragile Sinistcha/Incineroar duo. Piloting executed flawlessly with zero errors, allowing me to sustain offensive momentum through their consecutive Protect stalling. Between-game adjustments to lock in this aggressive weather-control and physical-pressure framework helped secure the win, as they denied their sweepers setup time and forced unfavorable early trades.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, I would retain the Froslass-Mega lead and Snowscape strategy but replace Kingambit with a faster, more durable pivot to better survive Incineroar's early Flare Blitz/Parting Shot cycles. When facing Floette-Mega's Protect-heavy stalling, I should prioritize faster priority users or multi-hit coverage earlier in the game to bypass Protect chains rather than relying on PP attrition. Maintaining consistent physical pressure and avoiding passive turns will prevent their Fairy Aura core from safely setting up CalmMind.
reflections.notebook:
- Floette-Mega relies on CalmMind/Protect stalling; expect consecutive Protects once mega evolved.
- Sinistcha/Hospitality provides early healing but is fragile to super-effective weather moves and Focus Sash is easily broken.
- Incineroar typically leads with Intimidate/Helping Hand or FakeOut/Parting Shot to enable Basculegion sweeps.
- Basculegion runs Adaptability with Aqua Jet/Wave Crash/Last Respects; highly vulnerable to super-effective physical coverage.
- Expect Sneasler/Kingambit as bench threats; maintain speed control and priority usage.
- Weather control (Snowscape/Ice) effectively disrupts their core synergy and forces unfavorable trades.
- Protect stalling cores require sustained damage output and faster priority rather than single-turn finishes.

reflections.summary: We lost Game 3 and the series 1–2. The main reason was our team preview's poor fit against the opponent's aggressive lineup, particularly their Lycanroc-Dusk. Our between-game adjustments backfired: we brought too many overlapping Pokémon (Kingambit, Basculegion, Froslass) and lacked a proper check to Lycanroc-Dusk. Our Incineroar and Sinistcha fell early to their attacks, and our Floette-Mega win condition was eventually overwhelmed by their Basculegion and Lycanroc-Dusk after we lost our other threats. The opponent's Kingambit and Froslass-Mega applied additional pressure, but Lycanroc-Dusk was the decisive factor.
reflections.adjustment: Against this opponent, we should bring a dedicated Lycanroc-Dusk check (e.g., a Steel-type or a fast special attacker) and reduce overlap with their team. We should avoid bringing Incineroar and Sinistcha, which are weak to their Lycanroc-Dusk and Kingambit. A team built to outpace their Froslass-Mega and Basculegion while handling Lycanroc-Dusk would be more effective. Our Mega Stone holder (Floette) was not sufficient as a win condition against this opponent.
reflections.notebook: Durable notes: Opponent's brought team: Kingambit (Defiant, Life Orb, Adamant, Kowtow Cleave/Sucker Punch/Swords Dance/Protect), Froslass-Mega (Timid, Froslassite, Blizzard/Shadow Ball/Thunderbolt/Protect), Basculegion (Adaptability, Mystic Water, Adamant, Last Respects/Aqua Jet/Wave Crash/Protect), Lycanroc-Dusk (Tough Claws, Focus Sash, Adamant, Close Combat/Rock Slide/Accelerock/Protect). They did not bring Sneasler or Scovillain. They Mega Evolved Froslass on Turn 2 and set Snowscape. Lycanroc-Dusk is a major physical threat with Close Combat and priority Accelerock; it can OHKO or heavily damage most non-resistant Pokémon. Kingambit has Defiant, making Parting Shot risky. Basculegion is a strong physical cleaner with Wave Crash. Our Floette-Mega was insufficient as a win condition. For a rematch, prioritize a Lycanroc-Dusk check and avoid team overlap.
